newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia asks rights body to prove riots report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia asks rights body to prove riots report.

text.p: The Indonesian government said on Friday it was surprised by a national human rights commission report that five people died in riots in Jakarta in July and 74 were still missing and called on it to prove the figures.
"The government had explained the July 27 events as they were. The government is surprised by the figures of dead and missing given by the rights commission," State Secretary Murdiono told reporters.
"Therefore, the goverment wants the rights commission to prove the figures with acceptable evidence," Murdiono said.
He added however that the government had no intention of intervening in the functioning of the commission.

Indonesia's official human rights commission said last week that it had confirmed at least five people were killed in the riots in Jakarta on July 27, the worst violence in the capital for more than two decades.
Deputy chairman Marzuki Darusman and Secretary-General Baharuddin Lopa, issuing the preliminary findings of the body's fact-finding team, also said 74 people were reported missing after the event.
The government has said three people had died and made no mention of any missing.
The commission also said 149 people, including security officials, were injured during the disturbances.

The riots started after police raided the office of the Indonesian Democratic Party in central Jakarta which was being occupied by loyalist supporters of the ousted party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, was replaced in June by deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi at a government backed congress in Medan, North Sumatra.
Lopa told reporters the deaths had been confirmed by doctors at Jakarta hospitals but the commission did not have complete details about where and when the five died.
